region.text: Lucca province, the Republic whose territories 'included the Garfagnana to the north'

ledger.note: 1160: Lucca buys its feudal rights from Welf VI. The city 'bought the feudal rights from Margrave Welf VI in 1160, hence became subject only to the emperors' (infobox 'Established: 1160'). The land is my reading.

region.text: Lucca province, the Republic whose territories 'included the Garfagnana to the north'

ledger.note: 1314: Uguccione della Faggiuola takes Lucca. 'In 1314, internal discord allowed Uguccione della Faggiuola to make himself lord of Pisa and then to conquer Lucca.' Drawn as a Pisan-led occupation; the page does not say the city was Pisa's.

region.text: Lucca province, the Republic whose territories 'included the Garfagnana to the north'

ledger.note: 1316: Castruccio Castracani becomes lord of Lucca. 'the citizens gave the lordship over their Republic to the ghibelline Castruccio Castracani' (infobox 1316-1328), 'the highest peak of the Republic's power'.
1316: the lordship of Castruccio Castracani begins (infobox 1316-1328); in 1325 Lucca's forces beat the Florentine army at Altopascio. The state continues.
1328: Castruccio's lordship ends (infobox 1316-1328); the republican form returns until the loss of the city in 1335.

region.text: Lucca province, the Republic whose territories 'included the Garfagnana to the north'

ledger.note: 1335: Mastino II della Scala acquires Lucca. 'Parma (1335) in Lombardy and Lucca (1335) in Tuscany' (the Scaliger page says purchased, Lucca 1339). The Lucca page says only that it was 'subsequently acquired by the Republic of Pisa and administered by its Lord, Giovanni Dell'Agnello' (no year).

region.text: Lucca province, the Republic whose territories 'included the Garfagnana to the north'

ledger.note: 1370: Lucca is free again. 'Having regained its freedom in 1370, Lucca returned to a republican government.' The Pisan hold is undated on the page, so the counterpart is my reading.
1400: Paolo Guinigi overthrows the republican government. Infobox: 'Paolo Guinigi overthrows the republican government starting a Signoria: 1400-1430.'
1430: the republican government is restored (infobox). Florence besieged Lucca in 1429 and again in 1430; the page gives no result.

region.text: Lucca province, the Republic whose territories 'included the Garfagnana to the north'

ledger.note: 22 January 1799: French troops enter Lucca. 'on 22 January 1799 the French troops entered the city, overthrowing the oligarchic republic'.

region.text: Lucca province, the Republic whose territories 'included the Garfagnana to the north'

ledger.note: 23 June 1805: the republic is disestablished and Napoleon takes over its government ('In 1805, the governance of Lucca was taken over by Napoleon'); the French authority is the Directory in 1799, the Consulate and then the Empire.

region.text: Lucca province, the Republic whose territories 'included the Garfagnana to the north'

ledger.note: 23 June 1805: the Republic of Lucca ends (infobox 'Disestablished: 23 June 1805'); Lucca is merged with Piombino into the Principality of Lucca and Piombino.

wars.name: Battle of Altopascio
wars.outcome: Lucca's forces under Castruccio defeated the Florentine army and chased it 'up to the walls of Florence'.
wars.note: No border change on the page.

wars.name: Florentine siege of Lucca
wars.outcome: Florence besieged Lucca in 1429 and again in 1430 'to take revenge on the republic'; the page gives no result and no 1433 treaty.

certainty.note: No page opened gives lines; the province is a reading.

sources.title: Republic of Lucca
sources.note: 1160, Uguccione 1314, Castruccio 1316-1328, Guinigi 1400-1430, 1370, 1799, 1805. Silent on area and on the Pisan years.

notes: Written from two pages. Unsettled: the extent (Lucca province is a reading; Garfagnana and the coast are named, Versilia is not, and the Este held part of the Garfagnana), the years of the Pisan rule (the page says 'subsequently ... acquired by Pisa' with no date; 1335-1369 has no keyframe because Lucca was under Verona and Pisa), who ruled between 1328 and 1335 (page silent), and the French years 1799-1805 (the Directory, Consulate and Empire are not distinguished; the principality of 1805 needs a dossier from eu-20). Gazetteer names: none.
